newsitem.title: USA: House lawmaker aims for electric bill vote in July.
newsitem.headline: House lawmaker aims for electric bill vote in July.

text.p: The chairman of the House energy and power subcommittee said Tuesday he was still hoping his panel would vote in July on a bill to open local electricity markets to competition.

"I'd like to do it in my subcommittee by July," Rep. Dan Schaefer, a Colorado Republican, told reporters after speaking to the American Forest and Paper Association about his bill to require states to break up electric utility monopolies.
But he added that he had "no commitment" from House Commerce Committee chairman Thomas Bliley, a Virginia Republican, on when the full committee might vote on the bill.

Schaefer repeated that he planned to hold a few more subcommittee hearings in June on power market deregulation, although he already held nine in the last Congress and four field hearings over the last month.
"We're just trying to make sure we've covered every base," he said.
Schaefer said a major obstacle to bringing the issue up in his subcommittee had been the members' lack of understanding of the $200 billion industry.
"They're beginning to understand it," he said, adding that "some of them didn't know a megawatt from a kilowatt."
Most lawmakers and industry officials do not expect Congress to pass sweeping electricity legislation this year, although Bliley has said opening local power markets to competition is a top priority.
